t: You're on Guilford Street in Bloomsbury, a road running east-northeast from Russell Square to Gray's Inn Road. Note the spelling: it isn't Guildford in Surrey. The street is named after Frederick North, Lord North, the 2nd Earl of Guilford, who was Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782 and is most often remembered for losing the thirteen colonies in the American Revolutionary War. Two other people are tied to the street. The watercolour painter and caricaturist George Shepheard died here, and an artists' model called Dolores lived here.
